newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish planes bomb Kurd rebel camp in north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkish planes bomb Kurd rebel camp in north Iraq.

text.p: Turkish warplanes bombed a major Kurdish guerrilla camp in northern Iraq on Thursday as military forces continued a cross-border operation against rebels in the region, state-run Anatolian news agency said.

F-4 fighter-bombers took off from the southeastern Turkish city of Diyarbakir during the morning and attacked the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party's (PKK) camp at Hakurk, the agency quoted officials as saying.
The emergency rule governor's office in Diyarbakir said it had no knowledge of the attack.
Anatolian quoted the officials as saying 101 rebels have been killed and one captured wounded in the operation since it began on Monday night. Two soldiers have been reported killed in the fighting.
On Wednesday, it said Turkish F-4 planes destroyed three PKK camps in the Sinath region of northern Iraq.
An official Iraqi newspaper condemned Turkey on Thursday for pursuing the rebels into Iraq.
"Such an operation is condemned and rejected," said Al-Thawra newspaper, organ of the ruling Baath party.
The PKK uses bases in northern Iraq outside Baghdad's control as part of its guerrilla war for self-rule in southeast Turkey. Turkish troops have crossed into Iraq several times in large numbers.
This week's operation began after PKK rebels in Iraq had fired on troops along the border near the southeastern town of Silopi.
The Turkish armed forces responded by crossing the border near Silopi in brigade strength, together with air support.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old armed conflict between the security forces and the PKK.
